transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… yeah, I guess I’m here because I’ve just been feeling really low for a long time. Like I wake up and it’s already there, this heavy gray feeling, before I even get to the clinic. I work as a medical assistant, so I’m around patients and rooms and schedules all day, and sometimes I’m like, I should be able to just push through it, you know? But it kind of follows me through the whole day.
How long have you been feeling this low?

Um… it’s been about two years, a little over that — like two years and two months, I think. It kind of started after the staffing changed at the clinic and my schedule got all over the place, rotating shifts and stuff. I remember because everyone was complaining about the new schedule, and I kept thinking I’d adjust, but… the low feeling just never really went away.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like, or has that changed over the past two years?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean… I still do some things I used to do, but I don’t know if I’d call it enjoying them the same way. Like, I’ll put on a show or scroll around, but then I end up thinking about work stuff or random things, like whether I forgot to restock a room at the clinic. So… yeah, I guess it’s changed some, but I don’t know exactly how to describe it.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities that you used to find pleasurable?

I don’t know if I’d say I’ve lost interest exactly. Like, I still kind of do things, but sometimes it feels more like I’m just filling time. I used to, um… I don’t know, hang out or watch stuff and actually feel into it, but now I’ll start something and end up thinking about random things, like something someone said at work or whether I’m supposed to be up early the next day. So… maybe? I’m not really sure what counts as losing interest.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that normally would bring you happiness?

I’m not sure if I’d say unable. That sounds kind of… absolute, I guess. Like, sometimes something funny will happen and I’ll laugh, but then it fades really fast, or I’m thinking about something else. It’s hard to tell because I’ll start watching something I used to like and then I’m like, oh, I should check my laundry, or I remember this one patient at work who got mad about paperwork, and then I’m not really paying attention anymore.

So… I don’t know. I don’t think I’m completely unable to feel happy, but it doesn’t really stick the way it used to, maybe.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite over the past two years?

I don’t know… I haven’t really kept track of it. Some days I eat normal, I guess, and other days I just sort of grab whatever’s around because I’m busy or I forget until later. But I don’t know if that’s an appetite thing or just my schedule.

Like at the clinic, sometimes lunch gets weird because someone needs vitals or a room has to be turned over, and then by the time I think about food it’s like… not even that I’m not hungry, I just didn’t stop. So, yeah, I’m not sure I’ve noticed a clear change over the past couple years.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns over the past two years?

I’m not really sure. I mean, my sleep is kind of all over the place sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s new or just… life, I guess. Like if I have an early shift, I’ll try to go to bed earlier, but then I end up thinking about whether I set my alarm or if I forgot something at work, like restocking gloves or whatever, and then I’m just lying there.

But I don’t know if over the past two years there’s been a clear pattern. Some nights are fine, some nights aren’t. I haven’t really tracked it or anything.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things?

I don’t know… guilt is kind of a big word. I mean, I’ll think about things I said or did and wonder if I made it weird, or if I should’ve handled something better, especially at work, like if I didn’t room someone fast enough or I forgot to put something back where it goes. But then sometimes it’s not even my fault, it’s just the clinic being backed up, you know?

So… I guess I do question myself, but I’m not sure if that’s the same as feeling guilty all the time. I haven’t really thought about it that way.
Have you had thoughts about death or dying at any point over the past two years?

I don’t really know how to answer that. Like, death is something you see mentioned around the clinic sometimes, not in a dramatic way, just paperwork or people talking about older relatives and stuff, and then I’ll think about how weird it is that everyone has all these appointments and forms and insurance things and we’re all just trying to get through the day.

But, um… for me personally, I don’t know. I haven’t really sat down and thought, like, “Have I had thoughts about dying in the past two years?” That sounds intense when you say it that way. I guess I’d need you to explain what you mean—like passing thoughts, or something more serious?
Have you ever had thoughts that you would be better off dead or that you wanted to die?

I… I’m not sure. That wording feels really heavy, like “wanted to die” sounds so definite. I don’t know that I think about it in that exact way.

Sometimes when people say “better off,” I think of, like, better off if I wasn’t in the way or if I didn’t mess something up, but then I’m thinking about work stuff again—like if a patient gets annoyed because they waited too long, even though that’s not really on me. And then I’ll go home and replay it, which is dumb because everyone at the clinic is stressed and nobody has enough time.

But, um… I don’t know if that answers your question. I guess I’m not really sure what counts as that kind of thought.
Have you had any thoughts about not wanting to be alive anymore?

I don’t know… I think I’m getting stuck on the wording. “Not wanting to be alive” sounds like such a specific thing, and I don’t know if I’ve had that exact thought or if I just get really tired of dealing with everything.

Like, sometimes I’ll come home after a shift and just kind of sit there, and my brain keeps going over dumb little things—like whether I put the blood pressure cuffs back in the right place or if someone thought I was being rude. And then it turns into this whole thing where I’m just exhausted by my own head, I guess.

But I don’t know if that’s the same as not wanting to be alive. I’m not trying to dodge the question, I just… I don’t know how to sort that out.
Have you ever had recurring thoughts about your own death?

Recurring… I don’t know. I don’t think I’ve had, like, a repeated thought of “my own death” in that exact way.

Sometimes my mind gets stuck on things, but it’s usually random stuff, like something I said wrong or whether I handled something at work the right way. And then I’ll spiral off into thinking about how people just go through these routines every day, and it’s weird how normal everything feels even when everyone’s stressed.

But about my own death specifically… I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it as a recurring thing, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past two years?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, I haven’t really been tracking it closely. My clothes mostly fit the same, I think, but then some jeans fit weird depending on whether I washed them, so I don’t know if that counts.

I don’t own a scale or anything. At work we weigh people all the time, and it’s funny because I’m around that stuff constantly, but I don’t really check my own. So… no significant change that I’ve noticed, I guess.
Have you noticed any changes in how active or energetic you are compared to how you used to be?

Yeah… I think that part has changed a lot. I used to be able to do stuff after work, like shoot hoops for a bit or mess around with electronics, like taking apart a controller or whatever, but now it’s like by the time I finish rooming patients and trying to catch up on charts, I’m just done.

And it’s not even only on workdays. Like even if I sleep late on a day off, or I tell myself I’m gonna reset, my body still feels worn out. I’ll look at laundry and it’s like this whole huge project, which sounds stupid because it’s just laundry, but I just don’t have anything left.
Have you had any periods over the past two years where you felt significantly better for a while?

Not really… not like a real break where I felt back to normal for a while.

It’s been kind of this same stretch for, I don’t know, a little over two years now—maybe two years and two months? It started around when the clinic staffing changed and my schedule got all rotated and weird. Like one week I’d be opening, then later shifts, and everyone was swapping coverage, and it just… never really settled after that.

I might have a day where things feel slightly less awful, but I wouldn’t say there was a period where I was significantly better.
Do you feel like you're unable to feel pleasure or interest in things that you used to enjoy, even if you're technically doing them?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. Like, I still do some of the same stuff, so I guess technically I’m interested? But sometimes I’ll start something and then get distracted by, I don’t know, my phone or thinking about work stuff.

Like with electronics, I used to take apart controllers, but half the time now I’ll get everything spread out and then realize I don’t even remember where I put the tiny screws, which is a whole separate problem because my room is kind of a mess. And then I’m just annoyed.

So… I don’t know if that means I can’t feel pleasure, exactly. Maybe it’s just harder to stay into things? I’m not sure.
Is your low mood present every day, or are there days when you feel okay?

It’s… pretty much every day, honestly. I mean, I can still get up and go to the clinic and do what I’m supposed to do, but I wake up already feeling low, like before anything even happens.

It’s like this heavy gray feeling is just there when I open my eyes, and then I’m getting ready, thinking about traffic or whether I packed food, or if my scrubs are clean, and it’s still there. And then it follows me through most of the day. I might get distracted for a little bit, like if someone at work says something funny, but I wouldn’t really say I feel okay. It’s more like… slightly less bad for a minute.
Has your low mood been continuous since it started two years ago, or have you had any breaks where you felt normal?

Yeah… it’s been basically continuous. I don’t really remember a stretch where I felt normal again.

It started, like I said, around when the staffing changed at the clinic and my schedule started rotating all over the place—openings, later shifts, covering random gaps. That was… about two years and two months ago now, I think. And since then it’s just kind of stayed there. Maybe a day is a little less bad, but not a real break.
Has your low mood been present for most of each day, nearly every day, for the entire two years and two months you've been experiencing it?

Yeah, I mean… it’s been going on about two years and two months now. It started after the staffing changed at the clinic and my schedule started rotating all over the place, like different shifts and all that.

I guess “most of the day” sounds really exact, but… yeah, that’s basically what it feels like. It’s not like I had a month or even a couple weeks where I was back to normal. It’s just kind of been there since then.
Has your low mood lasted for two years or more?

Yeah… it’s been more than two years. About two years and two months, I think.

It kind of ties in my head to when the clinic staffing changed and my schedule started getting all over the place—like rotating shifts and covering gaps and everything. I remember because I kept thinking it would settle down once the schedule got normal again, but… it just didn’t really stop.
